personas.persona: Maya, 16, Year 12 in Manchester. Picked "School & mates", played the 20-card session on her phone. Lives on TikTok and bails on anything that feels like a lesson.

issues.problem: The feed feels like a lesson. 9 of my 20 cards were 'guess the study' reveals, and every reveal opens with the same header, 'Here's what the research found.', followed by surnames and years (Lieberman et al., 2007; Slovic, 1993; Wohl, Pychyl & Bennett, 2010; Bryan et al., 2011). By card 6 it was a quiz in a revision guide. On TikTok I'd have scrolled away by the third citation.
issues.fix: In the feed builder, allow at most 2 'reveal' cards in any 5 in a row and put a choice or swipe card between them. In every reveal text, move the parenthetical citation out of the first sentence and into the 'Why?' fold (for example, emotion-naming-label-reveal becomes 'Naming it calmed it. Picking the word lowered activity in the amygdala, the brain's alarm.' and '(Lieberman et al., 2007)' goes to source/Why). Rotate the reveal header between 'Plot twist:', 'Called it?' and 'The answer:' so 'Here's what the research found.' doesn't repeat every time.

issues.problem: Brilliant hook ('one bad moment feel louder than twenty good ones?'). I thought of my mate straight away. Then the game is about a local power plant. Massive let-down, nothing to do with me.
issues.fix: Change game.prompt to: 'Your mate's been solid for months, then leaves you on read when you really needed them. Scientists tested how trust moves like this (with news about a power plant, weirdly). People rated 45 bits of good and bad news. Which moved trust more?' Change the first line of insight to: 'One slip from a mate feels huge because bad weighs more than good. But one slip rarely wipes out months of being there, and owning it fast wins most of it back.'

issues.problem: The hook says 'It's a year from now' but the scenario is a festival trip 2 months away. The 'right' answer, 'Someone couldn't get the days free', is a work thing. At 16 the real risk is a parent saying no.
issues.fix: Hook: 'Your festival trip already flopped. Before it even happened. Why?' In step 2, replace 'someone couldn't get the days free' (in the scenario and in the best option) with 'someone's parents said no'. Change the best feedback to: 'One message tonight (ask them to ask their parents now) settles it. Fix the cheap, fast risks first.'

issues.problem: The explainer talks to adults ('For most adults many of these are work weeks'). The try_today asks me to block 2 hours in a calendar I don't have. The life-in-weeks idea is heavy at 16, and the one line that could make it about me is about office workers instead.
issues.fix: In game.explain, replace 'For most adults many of these are work weeks, so one well-guarded week counts.' with 'A summer holiday is about 6 of them, so one well-used week really counts.' Change try_today to: 'In your notes app, write the one thing you'd be proud of doing next week and the day you'll do it. Screenshot it as your lock screen.'

issues.problem: Six statements before any payoff is too long for the 'Quick one' label. Then my result dot (Will 3, Skill 5, Door 5) lands outside all three circles, which looks like 'you're nowhere'. The 'Starting Line' result is one long sentence chained with semicolons, so I didn't read it.
issues.fix: Cut the questions to 3 (keep one per axis: 'I'd do this even if no one saw.', 'I know the first three steps I'd take.', 'I can get the time, tools or permission I need for this within a week.'). Rewrite results[''].text as: 'Nothing's fully lit yet. Normal, not a verdict. Do one move on your lowest pillar tonight: Will → write why it matters. Skill → 5-minute practice. Door → ask one person.' In app.js, put the dot inside the circle of the highest-scoring axis when no axis passes the threshold, so it never floats outside every circle.

issues.problem: I can't vote, so a voting study is the opposite of 'about me'. The lesson (one exciting study isn't proof) is great and very relevant to TikTok life hacks, but the card never connects the two.
issues.fix: Append to game.reveal: 'Same goes for every "become a morning person in 3 days" video on your FYP: one viral claim is a hypothesis, not proof.' Change the hook to: 'One tiny word change was meant to change behaviour. Then someone checked.'

issues.problem: The try_team line (a 'house, class or team rule') doesn't fit how my mates actually work. The midnight panic happens in the group chat.
issues.fix: Change try_team to: 'Agree in your group chat: no homework-panic messages after 10pm before a test. Try it for a week and compare how you feel in the morning.'

issues.problem: I chose 'School & mates', but the screenshots still say 'With others:', and several try_team lines mention meetings or a 'meeting or family dinner' (emotion-naming-label-reveal, circle-competence-venn). It quietly drops me back into the adult world.
issues.fix: Check that S.world === 'young' is set when the world picker is tapped (the screens show the non-young branch at app.js line 227). Add an optional try_team_young field to the schema. For emotion-naming-label-reveal, use 'Start your group chat or form time with a 30-second round: "Right now I feel ___ because ___." Anyone can say pass.'

personas.verdict: Some cards actually got me. The revision-vs-scrolling plan ('bag down → notes before phone') is a trick I'd really use. The 'is it you or the setup?' swipe made me feel less rubbish about my timetable. Smart wait vs dodge was spot on. Everything is kind and nothing shames me, and the helpline footer is subtle. But too many cards are 'guess what scientists found in 1993' about power plants, army cadets and voters. With all the surnames and years it turns into homework, and I stopped wanting the next one around card 8. Cut the citations from the main text, use fewer studies in a row, and make every scenario about mates, school and my phone, and I'd keep scrolling.

personas.persona: Radu, 44, engineering manager in Cluj, non-native English speaker, tired and a bit burned out. Picked "Work" in the world picker. Wants tools for tomorrow's standup and 1:1s, not school or hobby stories.

issues.problem: I picked Work, but only 4 of 20 cards are written for work (three-conversations, psychological-safety, attention-residue, reversible-doors). The other 16 are 'audience: all' and use school or hobby examples: essays, a 3-1 football match, 'a subject or course, learning an instrument', a dinner, a group chat. Also, view-feed-dark.png shows a teen card ('You're 16 and you all leave school at 18... days left with your mates') in the feed. For a 44-year-old manager this feels like the wrong app, and the 'Work' choice does not seem to change much.
issues.fix: In the Work world, rank audience:'work' cards first and never serve audience:'teen' cards. For 'all' cards, add an optional per-world text override in the schema (e.g. a 'worlds.work' block that replaces game.prompt, scenario or examples) and fill it for the most-served 'all' cards below. Check that the feed filter really drops teen cards when world=work (the 'school days with your mates' card should not show up).

issues.problem: The reflection loop (review a win, pick one change) is very useful for retros, but step 1 is a football match ('Your team won 3-1, but you missed two easy passes'). For me it's the wrong picture, and I almost scrolled away.
issues.fix: Replace step 1 scenario with: "The release shipped on time, but two small bugs reached production. On Friday you…". Options: "Celebrate the release and move on." (feedback unchanged); "Celebrate, then name one thing that worked and one check to add next sprint." (best, feedback unchanged); "Spend the weekend replaying the two bugs." (feedback: "Caring is good, but replaying isn't reviewing. Name the fix, then let it go."). Change step 2 scenario to "You presented to leadership. It went OK but felt flat…".

issues.problem: The prompt examples are school and hobby ('a subject or course, learning an instrument, getting fitter'). Also, the 'S' result tells a person with high skill to 'ask one person for the chance this week', which is advice for a missing Open door, not a missing Will. It feels copy-pasted and confused me.
issues.fix: Prompt: "Pick one work goal (a skill you keep postponing, a project stuck in backlog, a hard talk with your boss). Answer every line for that one goal." Results.S.text: "Skill scores high today; want and door are lower. First write one sentence on why this matters to you. If the why is there, ask one person for the time or chance this week."

issues.problem: This is the best card for me, but step 2 has only two options, so the right answer is obvious and there is no real choice. It also misses the most common manager mistake: taking the problem away from the junior.
issues.fix: Add a third option to step 2: text "\"OK, leave it with me, I'll handle the customer.\"", feedback: "Kind and fast, but they lose the chance to learn and may feel sidelined. Fix it together, and let them own the follow-up with your support."

issues.problem: The hook is great for a manager ('669 managers ranked... where did progress land?'), but the reveal ends with 'Same goes for school', which breaks it for work. Also the id says 'estimate' but the card is a reveal, which is confusing for editors. The helpline footer (from sensitive:true) on a card about motivation at work feels heavy.
issues.fix: Reveal last sentence: "For your team the same: one visible small win this week beats a big vague goal." Rename the id to small-wins-managers-reveal (or keep the id but note the type). Set sensitive:false unless the card mentions distress.

issues.problem: The tone is too much: 'ZAP THEMSELVES' in caps, plus '…but oof'. It also says '2 in 3 men' without saying how small the group was (18 men). As a skeptical engineer I trust the card less.
issues.fix: explain: "67%: 12 of 18 men pressed the shock button at least once rather than sit 15 minutes with their thoughts (women: 6 of 24, about 1 in 4), even though they'd said they would pay to avoid it. Small study (Wilson et al., Science, 2014), so treat it as a striking hint, not a law."

issues.problem: Every 'workable' example is from personal life (dinner, results email, group chat). There is no work feeling, but managers say 'I'm stressed' all day.
issues.fix: Replace the 'results email' item with: text "I'm frustrated because the deadline moved again and nobody asked me.", side right, why "Clear feeling plus cause. The next step is obvious: ask who decides deadlines and how you get a say." Replace the 'group chat' item with: text "I feel left out because the architecture decision was made without me.", side right, why "Specific feeling plus cause. You can check what happened, or ask to be included next time."

issues.problem: Step 1 examples are 'an essay, a tax form'. Step 2 changes from 'what do you do' to a trivia question about a ketchup drink, which surprised me and felt unconnected on a small screen.
issues.fix: Step 1 scenario: "You finally open the thing you've been dodging: a performance review to write, a budget sheet, a tricky message to a peer. 'Ugh, where do I even start?'…". Step 2: start with a bridge sentence: "Why do we push it to 'tomorrow'? Real study: …".

personas.verdict: Some cards I will use tomorrow: 'Thanks for telling me' in standup, the 'quick qs' note, and asking 'what are we missing?' and waiting 10 seconds. These are simple and practical, and they are kind, never shaming. But I chose Work, and most of the feed still talks about essays, football, school and instruments, and I even saw a card for 16-year-olds. That makes me feel this is not for me, and I start to scroll past. The research is honest about small studies, which I respect. Fix the per-world text and the feed would be very good for a tired manager. Now it is good, with too much noise.

personas.persona: Elena, 68, retired literature teacher who reads Seneca, Aristotle and Peterson. She values depth, accuracy and respect for the reader, and dislikes pop-psych oversimplification. Session 14, "Everyday life" world, 19 cards served. I looked at 12 screenshots: the a and b shots for responsibility-meaning, dichotomy-of-control, wso-triad (b), opportunity-cost (b), hedonic-adaptation (b), grit (b), still-water (a), useful-truth (b), plus view-feed-dark and view-tracks-light.

issues.problem: The reveal shows only the first sentence of 'insight' (app.js line 216, firstLine regex). The caveats that make these cards honest are pushed behind 'Why? 15-second read', which most people will not open. On responsibility-meaning I am left with 'Frankl found meaning in what we carry for others.' and nothing more: the Peterson Rule 7 line and the warning that a heavy week only counts if you can recover from it are hidden. On dichotomy-of-control the visible line is 'You didn't stop caring about getting home.', which means nothing on its own. Depth is being cut away by the layout.
issues.fix: In app.js line 216, show the first two sentences (match /^(.*?[.!?](\s|$)){1,2}/), or the whole insight when it is 220 characters or fewer. Also add an editorial rule to CARD_SCHEMA.md: 'The first sentence of insight must stand alone as the thesis and must contain the key caveat if there is one.'

issues.problem: 'Frankl found meaning in what we carry for others' is a misreading of Frankl, and as the only visible line it is the whole lesson. Frankl named three sources of meaning: creating or doing a deed, experiencing something or loving someone, and the attitude we take toward suffering we cannot avoid. Reducing this to 'carrying for others' turns logotherapy into a duty slogan, which is risky on a card marked sensitive.
issues.fix: Rewrite insight as: "Frankl named three roads to meaning: what we give or create, what (and whom) we love, and how we bear what we cannot change. Peterson's Rule 7 says pursue what is meaningful, not what is expedient. A heavy week only means something if you can recover from it." Change model to: "Happiness often comes from receiving; meaning often comes from giving, loving, or bearing something well."

issues.problem: Two problems. First, the visible line ('You didn't stop caring about getting home.') makes no sense out of context, and Epictetus only shows up in the hidden part. Second, the dichotomy of control is set out in Enchiridion chapter 1 ('Some things are in our control and others not'), but 'Read next' points readers only to chapters 5 and 8, so a curious reader misses the founding passage.
issues.fix: Rewrite insight as: "Epictetus opens the Enchiridion with it: some things are up to us (judgment, choice, next action), others are not (the plane, the seat). You can still care about getting home; you just put your effort where it is yours." Set from_source.next_read to "Enchiridion, chapters 1, 5 and 8 (short, free online)".

issues.problem: The feed does not fit the reader's age. view-feed-dark serves an 'Old Wisdom' card that opens with "You're 16 and you all leave school at 18". Several 'audience: all' cards in my Everyday-life session also assume a pupil: wso-triad 'a subject or course', procrastination 'an essay', habit-loop 'a lesson'. At 68 I feel I have walked into a classroom I left forty years ago. The memento-mori idea would hit me far harder with an adult number.
issues.fix: Add a one-tap 'life stage' option next to the world picker (Student / Working / Retired or later). Tag school-only cards audience:'teen' and filter them out for other stages. Also edit the wording on all-audience cards: wso-triad prompt to "Pick one goal (learning something new, an instrument, getting fitter, a hard conversation)"; procrastination step 1 to "an essay, a tax form, a tricky letter or message"; habit-loop step 2 to "something hard (a form, a lesson, a tricky message)".

issues.problem: In light mode the explanatory text (the insight line, 'With others', the disclaimer) is small, light-grey text on a near-white card, which is hard to read for older eyes. The parts that carry the thinking look the faintest on the screen.
issues.fix: Raise the secondary body text colour to at least 7:1 contrast against the card (for example #3F4654 on #FFFFFF in light mode), set its minimum size to 17px, and use the same weight as the reveal paragraph.

issues.problem: The insight line 'Being quiet isn't the fix on its own; asking for unshared facts is' is confusing: nobody proposed quietness as a fix. Susan Cain is listed as a thinker although the card is about Stasser & Titus's 'hidden profile' effect, not introversion, so the attribution blurs the lesson.
issues.fix: Rewrite insight as: "Groups drift to the facts everyone already holds, so a clue only one person has can go unsaid. The fix is a question: what does only one of us know?" Remove 'Susan Cain' from source.thinkers and remove 'Cain, Quiet (2012)' from source.work.

issues.problem: The card is filed under 'one_percent' but plays a doubling game (100% a day), then admits in the insight that habits don't double. The thesis contradicts itself, and the 'judge it at box 30' advice still implies exponential payoff. This is the kind of pop arithmetic I distrust.
issues.fix: Change model to: "Some growth hides for a long time before it shows. Habits don't double, but they do need weeks before you can judge them." Change try_today to: "Draw 66 small boxes. Tick one each day you do your tiny habit. Judge it at the end, not in week one."

issues.problem: 'about 40 C' is missing its degree sign, and the review actually reports roughly 40 to 42.5 °C. The imprecision is small, but on a card that cites a review it reads as careless.
issues.fix: Change the item's why to: "A 2019 review found a warm bath or shower (about 40–42 °C) taken 1–2 hours before bed helped people fall asleep about 10 minutes sooner."

personas.verdict: Better than I expected. The sourcing is careful: Wason, Drew and Wolfe, Brickman's small sample offset by Lindqvist, and the grit hype questioned openly. The primary-source quotes from Bacon, James, Epictetus and Hardin are real, well chosen and come with a 'read next', which is exactly what keeps a reader like me. The design works against that depth, though. The reveal shows only the first sentence of the insight, so careful caveats disappear behind a 'Why?' toggle, and on the meaning card what is left is a misreading of Frankl. The feed still talks to schoolchildren in my 'Everyday life' world, and the grey secondary text is hard on older eyes. Fix the truncation and the Frankl line and this would be a 7 or 8 for me. Today it is a solid, honest 6 to 7, more instructive than fun.

personas.persona: Sam, 24, graduate with anxiety and low self-worth after a rough year; picked "Everyday life"; sensitive to shame, labels and pressure.

issues.problem: In the screenshot (wso-triad-venn-a.png), when I score low on everything my dot sits outside all three circles, alone in the bottom-left corner. Even with 'not a verdict on you' underneath, the picture says I'm outside everything. That's the exact feeling I came here to get away from. 'Lowest today: Will' also reads like 'you lack willpower'.
issues.fix: When no axis reaches the threshold (result key ""), don't draw the dot in empty space. Put it in the centre with the label 'You, today: starting line', or hide the dot and keep only the scores. Change the score line from 'Lowest today: Will' to 'Easiest place to start: Will'.

issues.problem: The item 'You had a terrible week and feel like giving up tonight.' is ambiguous for someone who's struggling. 'Giving up tonight' can read as giving up on more than the project. The helpline footer sits far below the swipe, so it doesn't help much in the moment.
issues.fix: Change the item text to: "You had a terrible week and feel like quitting this project tonight." Change its 'why' to: "That feeling is real and worth hearing. One rough night just isn't enough to decide a project on. Rest first, then decide."

issues.problem: Try today says 'Pick one small thing someone relies on you for'. When your self-worth is low, it's easy to think 'nobody relies on me', and the card turns into proof of that. The insight line 'A heavy week only means something if you can recover from it' is confusing. It also suggests that weeks I didn't bounce back from were meaningless.
issues.fix: Change try_today to: "Do one small, caring thing for someone today (a message, a favour, holding a door), or one thing future-you will thank you for. Afterwards, notice how it felt." Change the last insight sentence to: "Meaning can be heavy, so rest counts too: carry what you can recover from."

issues.problem: Try today ('Pick one limiting belief. Try the smallest action that only makes sense if it's false.') is too abstract to act on when you're anxious. I couldn't work out what that action would be for my own belief, and the card gives no example.
issues.fix: Change try_today to: "Pick one belief like 'I'm not a people person' or 'I'm bad at interviews'. Do one tiny thing that only makes sense if it's false (say 'thanks, have a good one' to a cashier). Note what happened, no grading."

issues.problem: The numbers clash. The insight says habits take a median of 66 days (up to 254), but try_today says to draw 30 boxes and judge the habit at box 30. If I'm anxious, day 30 with no habit yet feels like I failed again, when the card's own data says that's normal.
issues.fix: Change try_today to: "Draw 66 boxes on paper (the median from the study). Tick one each day you do your tiny habit. Missed one? Just tick the next. Check in at box 30, but don't judge it until 66."

issues.problem: The result headline '3 of 6. Here's the pattern.' leads with my score on a card about feelings. On a card about naming emotions, a bare score feels like I'm being graded on my feelings.
issues.fix: For emotion-domain or sensitive swipe cards, put the pattern first and drop the score into small text. Example headline: "Here's the pattern", with "3 of 6 sorted" as a small subline.

issues.problem: The hook 'Your last focus session flopped.' assumes I failed before I've even answered anything. That's a small dig I didn't need.
issues.fix: Change the hook to: "Some focus sessions click, some don't. Which flow ingredient made the difference last time?"

issues.problem: The feed screenshot (view-feed-dark.png) shows a card written for a 16-year-old ('You're 16 and you all leave school at 18...'). For me at 24 in 'Everyday life' it doesn't fit, and it's a bit of a gut-punch about lost time. Separately, the Tracks screen leads with 'x / y played' progress bars, which feels like a completion checklist I'm behind on.
issues.fix: Filter cards with school-age framing (audience 'teen' or wording like 'You're 16') out of the Everyday-life world for adult users, or rewrite them in a neutral voice. On Tracks, change the counter to 'played x' and show the progress bar only after the first play in that track.

personas.verdict: This session mostly felt safe and kind to me. Most wrong answers get a 'fair guess' or 'very human' instead of a buzzer, the reflection and helpline footer shows up on the sensitive cards, and several cards gave me something small I could actually do tonight (name the feeling, then do 5 minutes; charge my phone across the room; wait for the delay). The weak spots are visual and wording slips that land hard on an anxious reader: my low-score dot drawn outside every circle, a 'giving up tonight' line that can be read the wrong way, a try-today that assumes someone relies on me, and a habit tracker whose day count contradicts the card's own data. Fix those and I'd keep scrolling and probably share the emotion-naming and procrastination cards.

personas.persona: Dr. Okafor, 51, research psychologist. Checks every citation, effect size and survey item. Played the "Everyday life" world in session 14 (20 cards) and looked at 12 screenshots.

issues.problem: The quiz still rewards the hyped headline. 'High-school grades' was never tested on its own: high-school rank is part of the academy's Whole Candidate Score. Saying grit 'beat' the admissions score is a hollow win, because that score did not predict finishing Beast at all. 'Dropouts were rare' hides the base rate. The caveats also arrive after the player has already been rewarded for the myth-shaped answer. The hook ('Talent or not giving up') sets up a false talent-vs-grit split.
issues.fix: Change choices to: ["The academy's own admissions score (grades, fitness, leadership)", "A 12-question grit survey", "Neither predicted it well"], keeping answer 1. Replace reveal with: "The grit survey, in one 2007 study of about 1,200 cadets. Only about 1 in 20 dropped out, and the admissions score didn't predict who did. But a 2017 review of 88 samples found grit's links to success modest, mostly via the 'keep going' part, and in a larger 2019 West Point study other measures mattered more for graduating." Change hook to: "Who survives the army's hardest summer? Guess what predicted it."

issues.problem: The result screen shows only the first sentence of the insight (renderReveal firstLine). On several cards that sentence is the overclaim and the caveat is the second sentence, hidden behind a collapsed 'Why?'. Visible in the screenshots: opportunity-cost loses 'hold it lightly', grit loses 'One ingredient, not the recipe', responsibility-meaning loses 'A heavy week only means something if you can recover from it' (a safety caveat on a sensitive card), and gorilla loses 'That's how focus works'. In the s14 screenshots 'Why?' is closed even though the code says it opens for the life world.
issues.fix: In renderReveal, show the full card.insight instead of firstLine when card.evidence is 'contested' or 'philosophy' or card.sensitive is true. Also add a CARD_SCHEMA rule: 'If the insight carries a caveat, it must be inside the first sentence.' Check why details.why rendered closed with S.world === 'life'.

issues.problem: The 'best' experiment measures the wrong thing. 'Not a people person' is a belief about my own enjoyment, energy or skill, but the outcome noted is 'did they chat back?', which mostly measures strangers' mood. A cold reply (common and random) would falsely confirm the limiting belief, which is a bad test design and a mild harm risk on a sensitive card.
issues.fix: Change choice 3 to: "For one week, try one tiny chat a day (even 'thanks, have a good one'). Before each, guess how it'll feel (1-5); after, rate how it actually felt." In the reveal, replace 'and note one fact: did they chat back?' logic with: "...a small experiment that compares your prediction with how it actually felt beats both. People often expect small talk to go worse than it does." Change try_today to end: "Write your prediction first, then what happened. No grading."

issues.problem: The correct option is double-barrelled ('About the same or a bit less'), so it merges two different outcomes and makes the right answer unfalsifiable. The reveal then states 'A bit less'. The hook ('a year later') is not what was measured: winners had won 1 to 18 months earlier and were rated once. In a sample of 22 the 'less' difference is fragile, and the card states it with more confidence than the data supports.
issues.fix: Set choices to ["More", "A bit less", "About the same", "Much less"] with answer 1. Hook: "You win the lottery. Do everyday pleasures get better?" Change the reveal's first sentence to: "A bit less, in one small 1978 study of 22 winners (Brickman et al.): a hint, not a law." Keep the Lindqvist twist.

issues.problem: Survey design: one item per axis on a 4-point agreement scale ('Not really / A bit / Mostly / Totally'). Item 4 ('I went 25 minutes without checking my phone') is a yes/no fact, so 'A bit' is meaningless. Item 1 ('knew exactly') is unclear when rated on a graded scale. The insight's 'Protecting focus from interruptions helps all three' is not a Csikszentmihalyi finding.
issues.fix: Item 1: "In my last focus session, I knew what 'done' looked like." Item 4: "In my last focus session, I stayed on the task without checking my phone or messages." Insight: "Csikszentmihalyi linked flow to clear goals, quick feedback and a challenge that stretches your skill a little. Fewer interruptions give those a chance to work. Fix the weakest one first."

issues.problem: On a card flagged sensitive, the item 'You had a terrible week and feel like giving up tonight' is ambiguous: 'giving up' can be read as giving up on life. The swipe then files it under 'Not a quit signal' with 'Rest first', which is the wrong response for a reader who means that.
issues.fix: Rewrite the item text to: "You had a terrible week and feel like quitting the team (or course) tonight." Keep side 'right' and the why text.

issues.problem: World filter leak: in the Everyday-life session, the gorilla card's 'Next' button offered the work-audience card map-territory-green-dashboard-choice ('Every status report says green. So why is your best engineer so quiet?'). Visible in goal-directed-perception-gorilla-b.png. Either S.world was not applied in this run, or the next-up target path skipped inWorld.
issues.fix: Make sure the life-world pick persists to S.world before the feed renders. Add a QA assertion that every next-up and related target passes inWorld(CARD[t]), and if none does, fall back to CONCEPT[cid].line with a same-world card or hide the button.

issues.problem: Attribution padding and an unclear insight. Susan Cain is listed as a source, but Stasser & Titus (1985) had nothing to do with introversion. The distractor 'Asked the quietest member first' and the line 'Being quiet isn't the fix on its own' imply a quiet-person mechanism the study did not test.
issues.fix: Remove 'Susan Cain' from thinkers and 'Cain, Quiet (2012)' from source.work. Change choice 3 to "Voted straight away without discussing". Change the insight's second sentence to: "Unshared facts surface when someone explicitly asks for them."

personas.verdict:
This is better sourced than most pop-psychology content I review. The Wason, Drew/Vo/Wolfe, Ferraro & Taylor, Pronin, Lally, Stasser & Titus and Hanoi-bounty figures check out. The doubling arithmetic is correct (A leads through day 13, B ends at about 1.07 billion). Contested findings (grit, regret, sleep-and-mood) are labelled honestly. The WSO Venn's inverted items invert correctly, and the results follow from the answers. The weak spots are craft rather than fraud:
- One quiz (grit) still rewards the myth-shaped answer before the caveats arrive.
- A few survey items are double-barrelled or binary questions put on a graded scale (flow, hedonic).
- One behavioural experiment measures the wrong outcome (useful-truth).
- The reveal screen shows only the first sentence of the insight, which systematically hides the caveats the writers took care to add.

The responsibility-meaning card also narrows Frankl to 'what we carry for others' (he described three sources of meaning) and asks two questions in one prompt; it deserves a light pass. Fix the first-sentence truncation and the grit reveal and I would trust this with students. As a scrolling experience it is pleasant and useful but not yet something I'd share unprompted.

personas.persona: Lina, 31, product designer (mobile games and learning apps). Picked "Everyday life". I played the 19-card session and looked at 15 screenshots: the venn, estimate, swipe, radar, reveal and choice cards, plus the feed and tracks views.

issues.problem: This is the first card of the session and it's the slowest. You have to pick a goal in your head, then answer 6 statements, two of them reverse-scored, so it's well past 30 seconds. On the result, my position is an unlabeled black dot outside all three circles, bottom-left. It reads like a rendering bug, not 'you are here'. The reward is a dense paragraph.
issues.fix: Cut the questions to one per axis: W 'I'd do this even if no one saw.', S 'I know the first three steps I'd take.', O 'I can get the time, tools or permission I need within a week.' (drop both invert:true items). Change the hook to 'Stuck on something? It's missing one of three things. Find which in 20 seconds.' In the app, when no pillar is lit (the '' result), put the marker below the Venn with a label 'You: start here', or leave the dot out. Shorten results[''].text to 'Nothing's fully lit yet, which is normal. Do one 5-minute move on your lowest pillar tonight, then replay in 7 days.'

issues.problem: The hook promises an answer ('Which flow ingredient was missing?'), but even answers get 'Even across the board: pick the axis that matters most to you'. The game hands the decision back to me, so there's no payoff. The hook also assumes my last session flopped.
issues.fix: Hook: 'Think of your last focus session. Which flow ingredient was missing?' Add a mid/tie result that still names one fix: 'No single gap today. Start with the cheapest fix: phone in another room for one 25-minute block. Interruptions drag down the other three.' Or break ties toward axis 3 (No interruptions) in the app.

issues.problem: Four options and then 'Your call. No wrong answer here.' Tapping felt pointless. There's no prediction to get right or wrong, so the reveal has no reward. Four options is also one too many for a 30-second card.
issues.fix: Make it a prediction about the data. Prompt: '...In a survey of ~400 adults, which pattern showed up most?' choices: ['A happier, B more meaningful', 'B wins on both', 'A wins on both'], answer: 0. Reveal starts: 'A happier, B more meaningful. In Baumeister's 2013 survey...' and keep the rest (correlation, not a rule; both count).

issues.problem: On the result list, my wrong sorts show an orange X next to perfectly good sentences like 'I'm anxious because I haven't opened the email'. At a glance the X reads as 'this feeling is bad', not 'you sorted this wrong'. On an emotions card that's not ideal. The wrong ones are also listed first, so the reveal opens with a wall of Xs.
issues.fix: In the swipe result rows, replace the X/tick icons with text: 'You said: Too vague → it's Workable' for misses and 'Workable ✓' for hits. List correct sorts first, or keep the original item order. Change the headline at 3 of 6 from 'Here's the pattern.' to '3 of 6. The vague ones are trickier than they look.'

issues.problem: The slider value shows as a bare '20', with no £. It also starts at 20, near the middle, which anchors my guess. With step 5 it doesn't feel like a test of the 0/10/40/50 trap.
issues.fix: Set game.unit to '£' if the app supports a prefix; otherwise end the question with 'What did you give up, in £?'. Change step to 10 so the real options (0, 10, 40, 50) are the natural stops.

issues.problem: On estimate cards the thumb starts around 40% of the range (40% on the gorilla card, 830 days on the feed card). That anchors my guess and makes it easy to submit without thinking. The You/Real comparison bar has no scale, so 'Higher than you'd think' doesn't show me how far off I was.
issues.fix: Show '?' as the value and grey out the submit control until the first drag. Under the comparison bar, add min/max tick labels (e.g. '0%' and '100%') and the gap ('You were 43 points under').

issues.problem: 'Spot on' with a sparkle, then the reveal hedges straight away ('in that one 2007 study... dropouts were rare... smaller than the hype'). The win deflates in the first line. The honesty is right; the order is wrong.
issues.fix: Reveal: 'The grit survey beat the academy's own admissions score at predicting who finished Beast Barracks. The catch: later reviews found the effect modest, and it's mostly the "keep going" part that matters.'

issues.problem: Mixed message. The game and the model sell explosive doubling, then the insight says habits don't double, and try_today asks me to judge a habit at box 30. I leave unsure whether my habit will 'look like everything' one day.
issues.fix: Model: 'Small daily effort looks like nothing at first. Judge a habit at weeks, not days.' try_today: 'Draw 30 boxes. Tick one each day you do your tiny habit. Don't judge it before box 30; many habits take about 66 days to feel automatic.'

personas.verdict: The feed is kind, honest and well sourced, and the strongest cards have tight, curiosity-gap hooks: the gorilla estimate, the hotel shower and the crypto 'regret test' trap. I'd send those to a friend. Safety is excellent: no shaming, caveats where they belong, and the 'snapshot, not a verdict' line is a nice touch. What lets it down is game feel. The opening venn card takes far too long and its marker looks broken. The radar and the happy/meaningful reveal promise an answer and then hand the decision back to me, so they have no reward. On estimate sliders and the swipe review, the visual feedback is ambiguous: an anchored start, an unscaled bar, and X icons that read as judging a feeling. Fix the payoff moments and this goes from a nice-to-scroll 7 to something people share.

app_issues.problem: The feed feels like a lesson. 9 of my 20 cards were 'guess the study' reveals, and every reveal opens with the same header, 'Here's what the research found.', followed by surnames and years (Lieberman et al., 2007; Slovic, 1993; Wohl, Pychyl & Bennett, 2010; Bryan et al., 2011). By card 6 it was a quiz in a revision guide. On TikTok I'd have scrolled away by the third citation.
app_issues.fix: In the feed builder, allow at most 2 'reveal' cards in any 5 in a row and put a choice or swipe card between them. In every reveal text, move the parenthetical citation out of the first sentence and into the 'Why?' fold (for example, emotion-naming-label-reveal becomes 'Naming it calmed it. Picking the word lowered activity in the amygdala, the brain's alarm.' and '(Lieberman et al., 2007)' goes to source/Why). Rotate the reveal header between 'Plot twist:', 'Called it?' and 'The answer:' so 'Here's what the research found.' doesn't repeat every time.
app_issues.from: Maya, 16, Year 12 in Manchester. Picked "School & mates", played the 20-card session on her phone. Lives on TikTok and bails on anything that feels like a lesson.

app_issues.problem: I chose 'School & mates', but the screenshots still say 'With others:', and several try_team lines mention meetings or a 'meeting or family dinner' (emotion-naming-label-reveal, circle-competence-venn). It quietly drops me back into the adult world.
app_issues.fix: Check that S.world === 'young' is set when the world picker is tapped (the screens show the non-young branch at app.js line 227). Add an optional try_team_young field to the schema. For emotion-naming-label-reveal, use 'Start your group chat or form time with a 30-second round: "Right now I feel ___ because ___." Anyone can say pass.'
app_issues.from: Maya, 16, Year 12 in Manchester. Picked "School & mates", played the 20-card session on her phone. Lives on TikTok and bails on anything that feels like a lesson.

app_issues.problem: I picked Work, but only 4 of 20 cards are written for work (three-conversations, psychological-safety, attention-residue, reversible-doors). The other 16 are 'audience: all' and use school or hobby examples: essays, a 3-1 football match, 'a subject or course, learning an instrument', a dinner, a group chat. Also, view-feed-dark.png shows a teen card ('You're 16 and you all leave school at 18... days left with your mates') in the feed. For a 44-year-old manager this feels like the wrong app, and the 'Work' choice does not seem to change much.
app_issues.fix: In the Work world, rank audience:'work' cards first and never serve audience:'teen' cards. For 'all' cards, add an optional per-world text override in the schema (e.g. a 'worlds.work' block that replaces game.prompt, scenario or examples) and fill it for the most-served 'all' cards below. Check that the feed filter really drops teen cards when world=work (the 'school days with your mates' card should not show up).
app_issues.from: Radu, 44, engineering manager in Cluj, non-native English speaker, tired and a bit burned out. Picked "Work" in the world picker. Wants tools for tomorrow's standup and 1:1s, not school or hobby stories.

app_issues.problem: The reveal shows only the first sentence of 'insight' (app.js line 216, firstLine regex). The caveats that make these cards honest are pushed behind 'Why? 15-second read', which most people will not open. On responsibility-meaning I am left with 'Frankl found meaning in what we carry for others.' and nothing more: the Peterson Rule 7 line and the warning that a heavy week only counts if you can recover from it are hidden. On dichotomy-of-control the visible line is 'You didn't stop caring about getting home.', which means nothing on its own. Depth is being cut away by the layout.
app_issues.fix: In app.js line 216, show the first two sentences (match /^(.*?[.!?](\s|$)){1,2}/), or the whole insight when it is 220 characters or fewer. Also add an editorial rule to CARD_SCHEMA.md: 'The first sentence of insight must stand alone as the thesis and must contain the key caveat if there is one.'
app_issues.from: Elena, 68, retired literature teacher who reads Seneca, Aristotle and Peterson. She values depth, accuracy and respect for the reader, and dislikes pop-psych oversimplification. Session 14, "Everyday life" world, 19 cards served. I looked at 12 screenshots: the a and b shots for responsibility-meaning, dichotomy-of-control, wso-triad (b), opportunity-cost (b), hedonic-adaptation (b), grit (b), still-water (a), useful-truth (b), plus view-feed-dark and view-tracks-light.

app_issues.problem: The feed does not fit the reader's age. view-feed-dark serves an 'Old Wisdom' card that opens with "You're 16 and you all leave school at 18". Several 'audience: all' cards in my Everyday-life session also assume a pupil: wso-triad 'a subject or course', procrastination 'an essay', habit-loop 'a lesson'. At 68 I feel I have walked into a classroom I left forty years ago. The memento-mori idea would hit me far harder with an adult number.
app_issues.fix: Add a one-tap 'life stage' option next to the world picker (Student / Working / Retired or later). Tag school-only cards audience:'teen' and filter them out for other stages. Also edit the wording on all-audience cards: wso-triad prompt to "Pick one goal (learning something new, an instrument, getting fitter, a hard conversation)"; procrastination step 1 to "an essay, a tax form, a tricky letter or message"; habit-loop step 2 to "something hard (a form, a lesson, a tricky message)".

app_issues.problem: In light mode the explanatory text (the insight line, 'With others', the disclaimer) is small, light-grey text on a near-white card, which is hard to read for older eyes. The parts that carry the thinking look the faintest on the screen.
app_issues.fix: Raise the secondary body text colour to at least 7:1 contrast against the card (for example #3F4654 on #FFFFFF in light mode), set its minimum size to 17px, and use the same weight as the reveal paragraph.

app_issues.problem: The feed screenshot (view-feed-dark.png) shows a card written for a 16-year-old ('You're 16 and you all leave school at 18...'). For me at 24 in 'Everyday life' it doesn't fit, and it's a bit of a gut-punch about lost time. Separately, the Tracks screen leads with 'x / y played' progress bars, which feels like a completion checklist I'm behind on.
app_issues.fix: Filter cards with school-age framing (audience 'teen' or wording like 'You're 16') out of the Everyday-life world for adult users, or rewrite them in a neutral voice. On Tracks, change the counter to 'played x' and show the progress bar only after the first play in that track.
app_issues.from: Sam, 24, graduate with anxiety and low self-worth after a rough year; picked "Everyday life"; sensitive to shame, labels and pressure.

app_issues.problem: The result screen shows only the first sentence of the insight (renderReveal firstLine). On several cards that sentence is the overclaim and the caveat is the second sentence, hidden behind a collapsed 'Why?'. Visible in the screenshots: opportunity-cost loses 'hold it lightly', grit loses 'One ingredient, not the recipe', responsibility-meaning loses 'A heavy week only means something if you can recover from it' (a safety caveat on a sensitive card), and gorilla loses 'That's how focus works'. In the s14 screenshots 'Why?' is closed even though the code says it opens for the life world.
app_issues.fix: In renderReveal, show the full card.insight instead of firstLine when card.evidence is 'contested' or 'philosophy' or card.sensitive is true. Also add a CARD_SCHEMA rule: 'If the insight carries a caveat, it must be inside the first sentence.' Check why details.why rendered closed with S.world === 'life'.
